patients.summary: Retired textile worker treated for right breast IDC in 2018 who joined the practice in 2021, had a bone-metastatic recurrence in 2022, then severe vitamin D deficiency with osteomalacia, cachexia and progressive disease, and moved to home hospice after a 2026 family meeting.

documents.title: New patient inquiry
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Daughter phoned on behalf of her mother, Mei Zhang, 64. Mother has had no regular doctor for several years, only her cancer doctors. Explained membership, fees and that insurance still covers labs and specialists. Daughter will help with paperwork. New patient slot given for 9/8 at 9:30, 60 min. Asked them to bring all pill bottles and any cancer treatment paperwork they have at home.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT
64F here with her daughter to set up primary care. Says she has not had a family doctor in several years; her care since 2018 has all been at the cancer center.

ONCOLOGIC HX: Invasive ductal carcinoma, right breast, diagnosed 2018. Right modified radical mastectomy with axillary node dissection 2018. Adjuvant chemo through a right subclavian port, then radiation to the right chest wall. Port still in. Finished treatment, now seen in surveillance by her oncologist. She does not know her stage or tumor markers; daughter thinks the paperwork is at the cancer center. Will request a summary.

PMH: as above, otherwise nothing she knows of.
PSH: R MRM with ALND; port placement.
MEDS: none.
ALLERGIES: sulfa (hives), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
FHx: mother had breast cancer after menopause, found at 55, has since died. Maternal aunt with ovarian cancer. Father with high blood pressure.
SOCIAL: Retired, worked many years in a textile mill. Married, lives with husband in Easthampton. Daughter close by and helps with appointments. Never smoked. No alcohol.

ROS: no weight change she has noticed, no bone pain, no cough, appetite ok.

EXAM: small, thin woman, pleasant, English fluent. Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Right chest: healed mastectomy scar, no nodularity along the scar or chest wall, port site clean. Left breast without mass, no axillary or supraclavicular adenopathy. Abdomen soft, no liver edge. Spine nontender. No edema.

A/P
1. Hx R breast cancer, treated 2018, in surveillance. Request oncology summary. Oncology owns surveillance imaging.
2. Family hx breast/ovarian cancer. Asked whether genetics was ever done; she is not sure. Will look in the oncology records.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c today. Hep C and HIV screen once, ok with her. FIT kit given. Flu shot when the vaccine arrives, nurse visit. Medicare starts next spring, will do the welcome visit then.
RTC spring, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hello Mrs. Zhang, your blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol all came back normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens are negative. Nothing to change. Please drop off the stool kit when you can. Best, your primary care physician

documents.title: Oncology treatment summary (outside oncology group)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
TREATMENT SUMMARY - MEDICAL ONCOLOGY
Patient: Mei Zhang  DOB 03/29/1957
Prepared at request of primary care.

Diagnosis: invasive ductal carcinoma, right breast, 2018.
Surgery: right modified radical mastectomy with axillary lymph node dissection, 2018.
Vascular access: right subclavian implanted port, placed 2018, maintained with periodic flushes.
Systemic therapy: adjuvant chemotherapy, completed 2018.
Radiation: adjuvant radiation to the right chest wall, completed 2018.
Current status: no evidence of disease at last surveillance visit. Surveillance visits every 6 months with yearly imaging of the left breast.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (urticaria), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis) - avoid IV contrast or premedicate per radiology.
Medications: none.

Please contact our office with questions.

documents.title: Records review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed oncology summary. No stage, receptor or genetics information included. Fine for now; she is followed there.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Screening questions negative. Influenza vaccine IM left deltoid (no injections or BP on the right arm per mastectomy). Tolerated, observed 15 min. She states COVID primary series done at a pharmacy this spring; card not with her, will bring next time.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative. Repeat in a year. Letter to pt.

reports.text: LEFT MAMMOGRAM, SURVEILLANCE. History: right mastectomy 2018 for invasive ductal carcinoma. Technique: standard CC and MLO views of the left breast. Comparison: prior study from last year. Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. There is no suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcification. Skin and nipple unremarkable. No axillary adenopathy in the imaged field.
reports.conclusion: No mammographic evidence of malignancy, left breast. BI-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual surveillance.

documents.title: Left breast surveillance mammogram
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Report received by fax from the cancer center's breast imaging service. Study date 11/30/2021. Negative, BI-RADS 1. Reviewed by PCP.

procedures.procedure: Initial preventive physical examination (Welcome to Medicare)

documents.title: Welcome to Medicare Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
IPPE. Turned 65 last week, Medicare now primary with a supplement.
Feels well. Walks to the corner store, does her own cooking. Last oncology visit in winter was fine per pt.
Functional screen: independent in ADLs and IADLs, husband drives. No falls. Hearing and vision fine with readers. Home safe, one-floor living.
PHQ-2 0.
Meds: none. Allergies: sulfa, iodinated contrast.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular. Chest wall unchanged, port site clean. No adenopathy. Spine and hips nontender. Gait steady.

Plan:
- PCV20 and first Shingrix today, left arm. Second Shingrix in 2-6 months.
- Colon: FIT negative 11/2021, repeat this fall.
- Breast: left side imaging per oncology, last one negative.
- Bone density: will raise with oncology whether they want a DXA.
- Advance directive: gave her the health care proxy form; she wants her daughter as proxy. Will bring it back.
Follow up 6 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - back and hip pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 3-4 weeks of aching between the shoulder blades and in the right hip. Worse at night, not better lying down. No fall or lifting injury. No leg weakness, numbness, bladder or bowel change. No fever.
PMH right breast IDC 2018, s/p MRM, chemo, chest wall radiation.

O: Vitals as charted. Tender to percussion over the mid thoracic spine. Right hip with discomfort at end range internal rotation, no deformity, bears weight. Strength 5/5 legs, reflexes symmetric, sensation intact. Gait normal.

A/P: New night-predominant thoracic spine and right hip pain in a breast cancer survivor. Recurrence in bone has to be excluded first. Neuro intact today.
- Called her oncologist's office while she was here; they will bring her in this week and arrange restaging imaging (they know about the contrast allergy).
- Return precautions reviewed with her and daughter: any leg weakness, numbness or trouble with urine or stool means the ED today.
- Will touch base after oncology sees her.

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of breast
conditions.note: right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, metastatic recurrence, stage IV, widespread osseous metastases

documents.title: Results from cancer center
documents.author: patient
documents.body: (written by daughter) Hi doctor, wanted you to know the scans and the biopsy at the cancer center show the breast cancer came back and is in many of her bones, including her back and the right hip. They called it stage 4. She will start radiation to her back next week and then a new treatment. They gave her stronger pain pills. We are all pretty shaken. Thank you for calling them so fast.

documents.title: RE: Results from cancer center
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I am so sorry to hear this, and thank you for letting me know. I've updated her chart. Her oncology team will lead the cancer treatment; I'm here for everything else, including help with side effects, and for all of you. I'll call in a few weeks to see how radiation is going. Please send me the names and doses of the new pain medicines when you have them.

Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Check-in call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Spoke with pt and daughter (speakerphone). Radiation to the thoracic spine finished last week, back pain noticeably better. Started a new IV treatment at the cancer center through her port. Hip still aches with walking.
Daughter read me the bottles, all from oncology: morphine ER 30 mg q12h, morphine IR 15 mg q4h prn (using 1-2 a day), senna 8.6 mg bid, docusate 100 mg bid, prochlorperazine 10 mg q6h prn nausea. Bowels were stuck the first week on morphine, better since the senna and docusate. Nausea mild, on treatment days.
No leg weakness or numbness. Eating less but ok.
Med list updated. Reminded her not to stop the bowel regimen while on morphine. Office visit in the fall, sooner if needed. Asked oncology to fax their notes.

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation letter, June 2022
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY - OUTPATIENT NOTE
Date of service: 06/02/2022
Referring: primary care

Ms. Zhang is a 65-year-old woman with a history of right breast invasive ductal carcinoma treated in 2018 with mastectomy and axillary dissection, adjuvant chemotherapy and chest wall radiation, who was sent back to us by her primary care physician for new thoracic back and right hip pain.

Restaging imaging (done without iodinated contrast given her allergy) shows widespread osseous metastases, including the thoracic spine and the right hip. Bone biopsy confirms metastatic carcinoma consistent with her breast primary.

Impression: Stage IV invasive ductal carcinoma of the right breast with widespread osseous metastases. No cord compression.

Plan:
- Palliative radiation to the thoracic spine, arranged with radiation oncology.
- Begin palliative systemic therapy here; regimen and schedule discussed with patient and daughter.
- Pain: morphine sulfate ER 30 mg every 12 hours; morphine sulfate IR 15 mg every 4 hours as needed for breakthrough pain.
- Bowel regimen: senna 8.6 mg twice daily, docusate 100 mg twice daily.
- Prochlorperazine 10 mg every 6 hours as needed for nausea.
- Follow-up in clinic with labs before each cycle.

Allergies: sulfa drugs (urticaria), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: June oncology letter finally arrived. Matches what the family told me in June and July. Problem and med lists already reflect it. Filed.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Timed between treatment cycles; oncology ok'd. High-dose flu, Shingrix #2 and bivalent COVID booster, all left arm. No reactions during observation. Shingrix series now complete.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with daughter. Four months into treatment for the bone recurrence. Back pain much better since radiation; right hip still sore with walking, uses a cane outside now. Takes the ER morphine twice a day and 1 IR most days. Bowels every 1-2 days on senna/docusate. Some nausea the day after treatment, prochlorperazine helps. Appetite down, has lost about 3 kg since spring.

Exam: thin, tired-appearing. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Port site clean. Mild tenderness over the right hip. No spinal tenderness today. Neuro grossly intact. No edema.

A/P
1. Stage IV R breast IDC with bone mets - per oncology, on palliative systemic therapy.
2. Cancer pain - controlled on oncology's morphine regimen. Oncology prescribes; we won't co-prescribe.
3. Opioid-induced constipation - controlled.
4. Weight loss - on treatment; encouraged small frequent meals, protein with each meal. Recheck weight next visit.
CBC/CMP today since she's here (oncology draws too). Flu, COVID and Shingrix done last month. FIT not repeated given active metastatic disease. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mrs. Zhang, your blood count is a little low, which is common during treatment. Kidney function is normal. The alkaline phosphatase, a bone enzyme, is up a bit, which goes with the bone involvement your oncologist is treating. I've forwarded the results to them. Nothing new for you to do.
